topics.name: Linear motion under a variable force

practice.stem: A particle P of mass 2 kg moves in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. The only horizontal force on P is a resistance of magnitude 4v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed. Initially P has speed 10 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 10e⁻²ᵗ, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of P at time t s.
parts.working: M1 Newton's second law: 2 dv/dt = −4v; M1 separate and integrate: ln v = −2t + c; A1 v = 10 at t = 0 gives v = 10e⁻²ᵗ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the speed of P to fall to 2 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by P in this time.

practice.stem: An ice-hockey puck of mass 0.5 kg slides in a straight line across horizontal ice. Air resistance and friction together are modelled as a single resisting force of magnitude 0.1v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. The puck starts with speed 20 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 20e^(−0.2x), where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the puck when it has travelled x m.
parts.working: M1 use acceleration v dv/dx: 0.5v dv/dx = −0.1v²; A1 dv/dx = −0.2v; M1 integrate: ln v = −0.2x + c; A1 v = 20 at x = 0 gives result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled when the speed has fallen to 5 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A car of mass 800 kg starts from rest on a straight horizontal road. The engine produces a constant driving force of 2400 N and the resistance to motion is 40v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the car after t seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest speed the car could approach under this model.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that v = 60(1 − e^(−t/20)).
parts.working: M1 800 dv/dt = 2400 − 40v; M1 separate: ∫ dv/(60 − v) = ∫ dt/20; A1 −ln(60 − v) = t/20 + c; A1 v = 0 at t = 0 gives result.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the car to reach 30 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A small stone of mass 0.2 kg is released from rest and falls vertically through the air. The air resistance is 0.05v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed after t s. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dv/dt = 10 − 0.25v and hence find v in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 0.2 dv/dt = 0.2(10) − 0.05v; A1 dv/dt = 10 − 0.25v; M1 separate and integrate: −4 ln(40 − v) = t + c; A1 v = 40(1 − e^(−t/4)).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the stone after 3 seconds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the terminal speed of the stone.
parts.working: B1 v → 40 as t → ∞.

practice.stem: A cyclist and her bicycle have total mass 80 kg. She rides along a straight horizontal road in Islamabad, working at a constant power of 240 W. The resistance to motion is 2v N, where v m s⁻¹ is her speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 80v dv/dt = 240 − 2v².
parts.working: M1 driving force = power/speed = 240/v; A1 80 dv/dt = 240/v − 2v, multiply by v.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest speed that the cyclist can approach.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the cyclist when her speed is 5 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A particle P of mass 3 kg moves along the positive x-axis on a smooth horizontal surface. It passes through the origin O with speed 8 m s⁻¹ and is subject to a resisting force of magnitude 6v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed when its displacement from O is x m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using acceleration in the form v dv/dx, show that v = 8 − 2x.
parts.working: M1 3v dv/dx = −6v; A1 dv/dx = −2; A1 v = 8 − 2x using v = 8 at x = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of x when v = 2, and explain why P never reaches the point where x = 4.
parts.working: B1 x = 3; M1 from 3 dv/dt = −6v, v = 8e⁻²ᵗ, which is never zero; A1 so x = 4 − 4e⁻²ᵗ < 4 for all t.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for P to travel from O to the point where x = 3.

practice.stem: A ball of mass 0.1 kg is projected vertically upwards with speed 15 m s⁻¹. Air resistance has magnitude 0.02v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the ball. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest height above the point of projection reached by the ball.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken to reach this greatest height.

practice.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg moves along a straight horizontal motorway between Lahore and Islamabad. Its engine works at a constant rate of 30 kW and the resistance to motion is 25v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest possible speed of the car under this model.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that 1200v dv/dt = 30 000 − 25v².
parts.working: B1 1200 dv/dt = 30 000/v − 25v, multiplied by v.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the speed to increase from 10 m s⁻¹ to 20 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A block of mass 2 kg slides on a horizontal surface. The total resistance to its motion is (4 + 2v) N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed. The block is set moving with speed 6 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the time taken for the block to come to rest.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the block before it comes to rest.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 0.4 kg is released from rest at a great height and falls vertically. Air resistance has magnitude 0.004v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the terminal speed of the particle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance fallen when the speed is 20 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 5 kg is projected with speed 12 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Air resistance has magnitude 0.5v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that, while the particle moves up the plane, v dv/dx = −(5 + 0.1v²), where x m is the distance travelled up the plane.
parts.working: M1 5v dv/dx = −5g sin 30° − 0.5v²; A1 divide by 5: v dv/dx = −(5 + 0.1v²).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance the particle travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.

practice.stem: A motor boat of mass 400 kg is moving in a straight line across a lake at 9 m s⁻¹ when its engine is switched off. The water resistance is modelled as 50v^(3/2) N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the time taken for the speed to fall from 9 m s⁻¹ to 4 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled in this time.

practice.stem: A train of mass 50 000 kg starts from rest on a straight level track. The engine exerts a constant driving force of 40 000 N and the resistance to motion is kv N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed and k is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that the greatest speed the train can approach is 40 m s⁻¹, show that k = 1000.
parts.working: B1 at top speed 40 000 = 40k so k = 1000.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the train to reach 20 m s⁻¹ from rest.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled in this time.

practice.stem: A particle of mass m kg is projected vertically upwards with speed 30 m s⁻¹. Air resistance has magnitude 0.01mv² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed, and acts opposite to the direction of motion. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest height reached above the point of projection.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when it returns to the point of projection.
parts.working: M1 downwards: v dv/dy = 10 − 0.01v², y measured down from the top; M1 H = −50 ln(1 − 0.001w²); M1 equate: 1/(1 − 0.001w²) = 1.9; A1 w² = 1000(1 − 1/1.9) = 473.7; A1 w = 21.8 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A racing cyclist and her bicycle have total mass 75 kg. She works at a constant power of 300 W on a straight horizontal track, and the air resistance is 3v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is her speed when she has travelled x m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 75v² dv/dx = 300 − 3v³.
parts.working: M1 driving force 300/v; M1 75v dv/dx = 300/v − 3v²; A1 multiply by v.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest speed the cyclist can approach, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled while the speed increases from 2 m s⁻¹ to 4 m s⁻¹.

practice.stem: A sledge of mass 0.8 kg slides across smooth horizontal ice in a straight line. It passes the point O with speed 20 m s⁻¹, and air resistance has magnitude 0.04v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 20/(1 + t), where t s is the time after the sledge leaves O.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find x in terms of t, where x m is the distance from O.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken to travel 30 m from O, and the speed at that point.

practice.stem: A package of mass 1 kg is dropped from rest from a hovering drone. Air resistance has magnitude 0.5v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the package t s after release. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 20(1 − e^(−t/2)) and that the distance fallen is x = 20t − 40(1 − e^(−t/2)).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The package is released 50 m above the ground. Show that the time T s taken to reach the ground satisfies T = 4.5 − 2e^(−T/2), and use an iterative method starting with T₀ = 4.5 to find T correct to 2 decimal places.

practice.stem: A puck of mass m kg slides in a straight line on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.2. In addition, air resistance of magnitude 0.1mv² N acts, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. The initial speed is 10 m s⁻¹. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the deceleration of the puck is (2 + 0.1v²) m s⁻².
parts.working: M1 friction μmg = 0.2 × 10 × m = 2m N; A1 total resisting force m(2 + 0.1v²), divide by m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the puck to come to rest.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled before it comes to rest.

practice.stem: A stone of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upwards with speed 20 m s⁻¹. Air resistance has magnitude 0.25v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the time taken for the stone to reach its highest point.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest height reached, giving your answer in exact form and correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A particle P of mass 0.5 kg starts from rest at a point O and moves in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. At time t s it is acted on by a single horizontal force of magnitude 4e⁻ᵗ N in the direction of motion. Its speed is v m s⁻¹ and its displacement from O is x m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find v in terms of t, and state the limiting value of v.
parts.working: M1 0.5 dv/dt = 4e⁻ᵗ; A1 v = −8e⁻ᵗ + c with v = 0 at t = 0, v = 8(1 − e⁻ᵗ); B1 v → 8.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed and the displacement of P from O when t = 2.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 3 kg moves in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface under a single force of magnitude 12/(t + 1)² N, acting in the direction of motion, where t s is the time. At t = 0 its speed is 2 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 6 − 4/(t + 1).
parts.working: M1 3 dv/dt = 12/(t + 1)²; A1 v = −4/(t + 1) + c; A1 v = 2 at t = 0 gives c = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which the speed is 5 m s⁻¹, and the distance travelled up to that time.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 1 kg starts from rest and moves in a straight line on a horizontal surface. At time t s it is acted on by a force of magnitude 4t N in the direction of motion and a resistance of magnitude 2v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dv/dt + 2v = 4t and hence find v in terms of t.
parts.working: B1 1 × dv/dt = 4t − 2v; M1 integrating factor e²ᵗ; M1 ve²ᵗ = ∫ 4te²ᵗ dt = (2t − 1)e²ᵗ + c; A1 c = 1 from v(0) = 0; A1 v = 2t − 1 + e⁻²ᵗ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled in the first 2 seconds.
parts.working: M1 v > 0 for t > 0, so distance = ∫₀² (2t − 1 + e⁻²ᵗ) dt; M1 [t² − t − e⁻²ᵗ/2]₀²; A1 2.5 − 0.5e⁻⁴ = 2.49 m.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 2 kg starts from rest at O and moves along a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface under a force of 6 sin 3t N, where t s is the time, acting along the line. Its velocity is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find v in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 2 dv/dt = 6 sin 3t; A1 v = −cos 3t + c; A1 c = 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest speed of the particle and the first time at which it occurs.
parts.working: B1 greatest value of 1 − cos 3t is 2; B1 when 3t = π, t = π/3.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the displacement of the particle from O at this time.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 2 kg moves in a straight line on a horizontal surface. At time t s it is acted on by a force of 4t N in the direction of motion and a resistance of 4v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed. When t = 0, v = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = t − 1/2 + (7/2)e⁻²ᵗ.
parts.working: M1 2 dv/dt = 4t − 4v so dv/dt + 2v = 2t; M1 integrating factor e²ᵗ; M1 ve²ᵗ = ∫ 2te²ᵗ dt = (t − 1/2)e²ᵗ + c; A1 c = 7/2 from v(0) = 3; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least speed of the particle, giving your answer in exact form.

practice.stem: A small robot of mass 5 kg starts from rest and moves along a straight horizontal track in a warehouse in Karachi. At time t s the resultant force on it is 10/(1 + t) N in the direction of motion. Its speed is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find v in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 5 dv/dt = 10/(1 + t); A1 v = 2 ln(1 + t) using v(0) = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which v = 4 and the distance travelled up to that time, giving the distance in exact form.
parts.working: B1 t = e² − 1; M1 x = ∫ 2 ln(1 + t) dt by parts; A1 x = 2[(1 + t) ln(1 + t) − t]; M1 substitute t = e² − 1: 2[2e² − e² + 1]; A1 2(e² + 1) = 16.8 m.

practice.stem: A particle P of mass 0.5 kg moves along the x-axis. It starts from rest at the origin O and is acted on by a force of (4 − 2x) N in the positive x-direction, where x m is its displacement from O. Its speed is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v² = 16x − 4x².
parts.working: M1 0.5v dv/dx = 4 − 2x; M1 integrate: v²/4 = 4x − x² + c; A1 c = 0, v² = 16x − 4x².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest speed of P and the value of x at which P next comes to rest.
parts.working: M1 force zero (or v² greatest) at x = 2; A1 v² = 32 − 16 = 16, v = 4; B1 v = 0 when x = 4.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 1.5 kg starts from rest at a point O and moves along a straight line. When its displacement from O is x m, the only force acting on it is 3/(x + 1)² N directed away from O. Its speed is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v² = 4x/(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when x = 3, and state the value that the speed approaches as x increases.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 1 kg moves along the positive x-axis. It is projected from the origin O with speed 5 m s⁻¹ in the positive x-direction. When its displacement from O is x m, it is acted on by a single force of magnitude (2x + 3x²) N directed towards O. Its speed is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v² = 25 − 2x² − 2x³.
parts.working: M1 v dv/dx = −(2x + 3x²); M1 v²/2 = −x² − x³ + c; A1 c = 12.5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance from O at which the particle first comes to instantaneous rest, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 x³ + x² = 12.5; M1 numerical method, e.g. f(x) = x³ + x² − 12.5 changes sign between 2.025 and 2.035 (or iteration); A1 2.03 m.

practice.stem: A probe of mass m kg is launched vertically upwards from the surface of the Earth with speed 4000 m s⁻¹. When the probe is at distance x m from the centre of the Earth, the gravitational force on it is mgR²/x² N, where R = 6.4 × 10⁶ m is the radius of the Earth and g = 10 m s⁻². Air resistance is ignored. The speed of the probe is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that, while the probe is moving upwards, v dv/dx = −gR²/x².
parts.working: B1 mv dv/dx = −mgR²/x², divide by m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest height above the Earth's surface reached by the probe. Give your answer in kilometres, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 integrate: v²/2 = gR²/x + c; M1 at x = R, v = 4000: c = 8 × 10⁶ − gR; M1 v = 0: gR²/X = gR − 8 × 10⁶; A1 X = 7.314 × 10⁶ m; A1 height X − R = 914 km.

practice.stem: A particle of mass 2 kg moves along the positive x-axis. It is released from rest at the point where x = 2. When its displacement from the origin O is x m, the only force acting on it is an attraction towards O of magnitude 32/x³ N. Its speed is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v² = 4(4 − x²)/x².
parts.working: M1 2v dv/dx = −32/x³; M1 v²/2 = 8/x² + c; A1 c = −2 from v = 0 at x = 2, so v² = 16/x² − 4 = 4(4 − x²)/x².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when x = 1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the particle to move from x = 2 to x = 1.

practice.stem: The equation 2x³ − 5x² + 3x − 7 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ².
parts.working: M1 α² + β² + γ² = (Σα)² − 2Σαβ with Σα = 5/2, Σαβ = 3/2; A1 25/4 − 3 = 13/4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + 4x² − 2x + 9 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α² = (αβ + βγ + γα)² − 2αβγ(α + β + γ), and hence find its value.
parts.working: M1 expand (Σαβ)² = Σα²β² + 2αβγΣα; B1 Σα = −4, Σαβ = −2, αβγ = −9; A1 4 − 2(−9)(−4) = −68.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of 1/α² + 1/β² + 1/γ².

practice.stem: The equation 3x³ − x² + 6x + 2 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of (α + 1)(β + 1)(γ + 1).
parts.working: M1 expand: αβγ + Σαβ + Σα + 1 with Σα = 1/3, Σαβ = 2, αβγ = −2/3; A1 8/3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ².

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain what your answer to part (b) tells you about the roots of the equation.
parts.answer: Not all roots are real: one real root and two non-real (complex conjugate) roots.
parts.working: B1 sum of squares of real numbers cannot be negative, so the roots are not all real; real coefficients so exactly one real root and a conjugate pair.

practice.stem: The equation x⁴ − 3x³ + 5x − 2 = 0 has roots α, β, γ and δ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the values of Σα, Σαβ, Σαβγ and αβγδ.
parts.working: B2 all four correct (B1 for two or three correct).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ² + δ².

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ + 1/δ.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 6x² + kx − 10 = 0, where k is a constant, has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that α² + β² + γ² = 20, find the value of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + 2x² + 7x − 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ².

parts.label: b
parts.text: By using the fact that α³ = −2α² − 7α + 3, find the value of α³ + β³ + γ³.
parts.working: M1 sum the relation over all three roots: Σα³ = −2Σα² − 7Σα + 9; M1 substitute Σα² = −10, Σα = −2; A1 20 + 14 + 9 = 43.

practice.stem: The equation 4x³ + 8x² − x + 5 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of α/(βγ) + β/(γα) + γ/(αβ).
parts.working: M1 common denominator αβγ: (α² + β² + γ²)/αβγ with αβγ = −5/4; A1 −18/5.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ. Let Sₙ = αⁿ + βⁿ + γⁿ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that S₍ₙ₊₃₎ = 2S₍ₙ₊₂₎ − 5S₍ₙ₊₁₎ − Sₙ.
parts.working: M1 multiply x³ = 2x² − 5x − 1 by xⁿ and substitute each root; A1 add the three equations to obtain the result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of S₂, S₃ and S₄.
parts.working: B1 S₀ = 3, S₁ = 2; B1 S₂ = 4 − 10 = −6; M1 S₃ = 2S₂ − 5S₁ − S₀ = −25; A1 S₄ = 2S₃ − 5S₂ − S₁ = −22.

practice.stem: The equation 2x⁴ + x³ − 4x² + 3x − 6 = 0 has roots α, β, γ and δ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ² + δ².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of α³ + β³ + γ³ + δ³.
parts.working: M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3(Σα)(Σαβ) + 3Σαβγ, with Σαβγ = −3/2; M1 correct substitution; A1 −1/8 − 3 − 9/2 = −61/8.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of 1/α² + 1/β² + 1/γ² + 1/δ².

practice.stem: The roots of the equation x³ − 14x² + kx − 64 = 0, where k is a real constant, are real and in geometric progression.

parts.label: a
parts.text: By writing the roots as a/r, a and ar, show that a = 4.
parts.working: M1 product of roots a³ = 64; A1 a = 4 (real).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of k and the three roots.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = 4: 64 − 224 + 4k − 64 = 0; A1 k = 56; M1 other two roots have sum 14 − 4 = 10 and product 64/4 = 16; A1 roots 2, 4, 8.

practice.stem: The equation 2x³ − 9x² + kx − 3 = 0, where k is a constant, has three real roots in arithmetic progression.

parts.label: a
parts.text: By writing the roots as a − d, a and a + d, find the value of a.
parts.working: M1 sum of roots 3a = 9/2; A1 a = 3/2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of k.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact values of the other two roots.
parts.working: M1 product of roots (3/2)(a² − d²) = 3/2 so a² − d² = 1; M1 d² = 9/4 − 1 = 5/4; A1 roots 3/2 ± √5/2.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 3x² + 4x − 5 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α³ + β³ + γ³.
parts.working: B1 Σα = 3, Σαβ = 4, αβγ = 5; M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3αβγ; A1 27 − 36 + 15 = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The matrix M has rows (α, β, γ), (β, γ, α) and (γ, α, β). Show that det M = 3αβγ − (α³ + β³ + γ³) and hence find the value of det M.
parts.working: M1 expand det M = α(γβ − α²) − β(β² − αγ) + γ(αβ − γ²); A1 = 3αβγ − Σα³; A1 15 − 6 = 9.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + 5x² − 3x + 2 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that α²β + α²γ + β²α + β²γ + γ²α + γ²β = (α + β + γ)(αβ + βγ + γα) − 3αβγ, and find its value.
parts.working: M1 expand (Σα)(Σαβ) to get the six terms plus 3αβγ; A1 shown; A1 (−5)(−3) − 3(−2) = 21.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of α/β + β/α + β/γ + γ/β + γ/α + α/γ.
parts.working: M1 common denominator αβγ gives (sum in (a))/αβγ; A1 21/(−2) = −21/2.

practice.stem: The numbers α, β and γ satisfy α + β + γ = 3, α² + β² + γ² = 17 and α³ + β³ + γ³ = 27.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of αβ + βγ + γα and αβγ.
parts.working: M1 Σαβ = ((Σα)² − Σα²)/2 = (9 − 17)/2; A1 −4; M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3αβγ: 27 = 27 + 36 + 3αβγ; A1 αβγ = −12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find a cubic equation with integer coefficients whose roots are α, β and γ, and solve it.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + 2x² − x + 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ².

parts.label: b
parts.text: By writing α + β = −2 − γ, or otherwise, find the value of (α + β)² + (β + γ)² + (γ + α)².

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of (α + β)(β + γ)(γ + α).
parts.working: M1 Π(−2 − γ) = −Π(2 + γ) = −(8 + 4Σγ + 2Σαβ + αβγ) with αβγ = −3; A1 5.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − x + 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α⁴ + β⁴ + γ⁴.
parts.working: M1 α⁴ = α² − 4α from x³ = x − 4; M1 Σα⁴ = Σα² − 4Σα with Σα = 0, Σα² = 0 − 2(−1) = 2; A1 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the equation whose roots are 1/α, 1/β, 1/γ is 4y³ − y² + 1 = 0.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = 1/y: 1/y³ − 1/y + 4 = 0; A1 multiply by y³: 4y³ − y² + 1 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of 1/α³ + 1/β³ + 1/γ³.
parts.working: M1 for the new equation Σ1/α = 1/4, Σ1/(αβ) = 0, Π1/α = −1/4; M1 Σy³ = (Σy)³ − 3ΣyΣyz + 3Πy; A1 1/64 − 3/4 = −47/64.

practice.stem: The equation x⁴ + 2x³ − 3x² + x + 5 = 0 has roots α, β, γ and δ. Let Sₙ = αⁿ + βⁿ + γⁿ + δⁿ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of S₂ and S₃.
parts.working: B1 Σα = −2, Σαβ = −3, Σαβγ = −1, αβγδ = 5; A1 S₂ = 4 + 6 = 10; M1 S₃ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3Σαβγ; A1 −8 − 18 − 3 = −29.

parts.label: b
parts.text: By summing the equation over all four roots after multiplying it by suitable powers of x, find S₄.
parts.working: M1 x⁴ = −2x³ + 3x² − x − 5 so S₄ = −2S₃ + 3S₂ − S₁ − 5S₀ with S₀ = 4, S₁ = −2; M1 substitution: 58 + 30 + 2 − 20; A1 70.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + ax² + bx − 6 = 0, where a and b are real constants, has roots α, β and γ. It is given that α² + β² + γ² = 14 and 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ = 11/6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that αβ + βγ + γα = 11.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the two possible values of a.
parts.working: M1 (Σα)² = Σα² + 2Σαβ = 14 + 22 = 36; A1 Σα = ±6; A1 a = −Σα so a = −6 or 6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given also that all three roots are positive, find the roots.
parts.working: M1 positive roots so Σα = 6, a = −6: x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 = 0; A1 (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 so 1, 2, 3.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + 3x² − 2x − 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the sum of the products in pairs of αβ, βγ and γα is αβγ(α + β + γ), and write down the product αβ·βγ·γα in terms of αβγ.
parts.answer: αβ·βγ + βγ·γα + γα·αβ = αβγ(α + β + γ); product = (αβγ)²
parts.working: B1 each pair product contains αβγ times one root; B1 (αβγ)².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of (αβ)³ + (βγ)³ + (γα)³.
parts.working: B1 Σα = −3, Σαβ = −2, αβγ = 1; M1 for u = αβ etc: Σu = −2, Σuv = 1 × (−3) = −3, Πu = 1; M1 Σu³ = (Σu)³ − 3ΣuΣuv + 3Πu; A1 −8 − 18 + 3 = −23.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of α² + β² + γ² and α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α².
parts.answer: α² + β² + γ² = −2, α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α² = −7

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of (α² + 1)(β² + 1)(γ² + 1).
parts.working: M1 expand: α²β²γ² + Σα²β² + Σα² + 1; A1 16 − 7 − 2 + 1 = 8.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Verify your answer to part (b) by considering p(i)p(−i), where p(x) = x³ − 2x² + 3x − 4 and i² = −1.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 4x + 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ. Let Sₙ = αⁿ + βⁿ + γⁿ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that S₍ₙ₊₃₎ = 4S₍ₙ₊₁₎ − Sₙ.
parts.working: M1 multiply α³ = 4α − 1 by αⁿ; A1 sum over α, β, γ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of S₂, S₃ and S₅.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α²(β³ + γ³) + β²(γ³ + α³) + γ²(α³ + β³).
parts.working: M1 expression = S₂S₃ − S₅; A1 8(−3) − (−20) = −4.

practice.stem: The equation x⁴ + x² + 2x + 6 = 0 has roots α, β, γ and δ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ² + δ² and deduce that the equation has at least two non-real roots.
parts.working: B1 Σα = 0, Σαβ = 1; B1 Σα² = −2; B1 a negative sum of squares means not all roots are real, and with real coefficients non-real roots come in conjugate pairs, so at least two.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of α³ + β³ + γ³ + δ³.
parts.working: M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3Σαβγ with Σαβγ = −2; A1 −6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of α⁴ + β⁴ + γ⁴ + δ⁴.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 3x² + 5x − 2 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the cubic equation whose roots are 2α, 2β and 2γ.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = y/2: y³/8 − 3y²/4 + 5y/2 − 2 = 0; A1 multiply by 8: y³ − 6y² + 20y − 16 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your equation to find the value of 1/(2α) + 1/(2β) + 1/(2γ).
parts.working: M1 sum of reciprocals of new roots = 20/16; A1 5/4.

practice.stem: The equation 2x³ + x² − 4x + 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation whose roots are 1/α, 1/β and 1/γ is 3y³ − 4y² + y + 2 = 0.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = 1/y; A1 multiply through by y³: 2 + y − 4y² + 3y³ = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of 1/α² + 1/β² + 1/γ².
parts.working: M1 for the new equation Σ1/α = 4/3, Σ1/(αβ) = 1/3; M1 (4/3)² − 2(1/3); A1 10/9.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + 2x² − 3x + 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using the substitution y = x − 1, find the cubic equation whose roots are α − 1, β − 1 and γ − 1.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = y + 1; M1 expand (y + 1)³ + 2(y + 1)² − 3(y + 1) + 1; A1 y³ + 5y² + 4y + 1 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of (α − 1)(β − 1)(γ − 1) and of 1/(α − 1) + 1/(β − 1) + 1/(γ − 1).
parts.working: B1 product of new roots = −1; M1 sum of reciprocals = (sum of products in pairs)/(product) = 4/(−1); A1 −4.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 4x² + x + 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using the substitution y = x², show that the equation whose roots are α², β², γ² is y³ − 14y² + 25y − 9 = 0.
parts.working: M1 x³ + x = 4x² − 3, i.e. x(x² + 1) = 4x² − 3; M1 square both sides: x²(x² + 1)² = (4x² − 3)²; M1 replace x² by y: y(y + 1)² = (4y − 3)²; A1 y³ − 14y² + 25y − 9 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of α⁴ + β⁴ + γ⁴.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + x² − 2x + 5 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why β + γ = −1 − α.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the cubic equation with roots β + γ, γ + α and α + β.
parts.working: M1 y = −1 − x, so substitute x = −1 − y; M1 expand (−1 − y)³ + (−1 − y)² − 2(−1 − y) + 5 = 0; A1 y³ + 2y² − y − 7 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence write down the value of (α + β)(β + γ)(γ + α).
parts.working: B1 product of roots of the new equation = 7.

practice.stem: The equation 3x³ − 2x² + x − 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that if y = x/(x + 1) then x = y/(1 − y).
parts.working: B1 y(x + 1) = x so x(1 − y) = y.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the cubic equation, with integer coefficients, whose roots are α/(α + 1), β/(β + 1) and γ/(γ + 1).
parts.working: M1 substitute x = y/(1 − y); M1 multiply by (1 − y)³: 3y³ − 2y²(1 − y) + y(1 − y)² − 4(1 − y)³ = 0; M1 expand; A1 10y³ − 16y² + 13y − 4 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α/(α + 1) + β/(β + 1) + γ/(γ + 1).
parts.working: B1 sum of roots = 8/5.

practice.stem: The equation x³ − 2x + 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why αβ = −4/γ.
parts.working: B1 product of roots = −d/a = −4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that the equation whose roots are αβ, βγ and γα is y³ + 2y² − 16 = 0.
parts.working: M1 the new roots are −4/x for each root x, so substitute x = −4/y; M1 −64/y³ + 8/y + 4 = 0; A1 multiply by y³/4: y³ + 2y² − 16 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α².
parts.working: M1 Σu² = (Σu)² − 2Σuv with Σu = −2, Σuv = 0; A1 4.

practice.stem: The equation x³ + x − 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that α³ = 3 − α.
parts.working: B1 α satisfies α³ + α − 3 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the cubic equation whose roots are α³, β³ and γ³.
parts.working: M1 y = 3 − x, so substitute x = 3 − y; M1 (3 − y)³ + (3 − y) − 3 = 0; A1 y³ − 9y² + 28y − 27 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α⁶ + β⁶ + γ⁶.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass 2 kg, moving with speed 5 m s⁻¹, strikes sphere B, of mass 3 kg, which is at rest. Before impact, A's velocity makes an angle of 60° with the line of centres. The coefficient of restitution is 0.5. Find the speed of B after the collision.
parts.working: B1 component of A along line 5cos 60° = 2.5; M1 momentum 2(2.5) = 2v_A + 3v_B; M1 restitution v_B − v_A = 0.5(2.5); A1 v_B = 1.50.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of A after the collision and the angle its new direction makes with the line of centres.
parts.answer: 4.34 m s⁻¹ at 86.7° to the line of centres
parts.working: B1 v_A = 0.250, perpendicular component unchanged 5sin 60° = 4.33; M1 speed √(v_A² + 4.33²); A1 4.34 m s⁻¹, 86.7°.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two spheres A and B each have mass m. B is at rest and A moves with speed 6 m s⁻¹ at 30° to the line of centres when they collide. The collision is perfectly elastic (e = 1). Find the velocity components of A and of B after the collision, along and perpendicular to the line of centres.
parts.answer: A: 0 along, 3 m s⁻¹ perpendicular; B: 3√3 m s⁻¹ along the line, 0 perpendicular
parts.working: B1 components of A: 6cos 30° = 3√3 along, 3 perpendicular; M1 momentum m(3√3) = mv_A + mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = 3√3; A1 v_A = 0, v_B = 3√3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that A and B move off at right angles to each other, and that kinetic energy is conserved.
parts.working: B1 A moves perpendicular to the line, B along it; B1 ½m(27 + 9) = ½m(9) + ½m(27).

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Spheres A and B have equal mass. B is at rest. A moves with speed u in a direction making an angle α with the line of centres, where tan α = ¾. The coefficient of restitution is ⅔. Find, in terms of u, the speeds of A and B after the collision.
parts.working: B1 components 4u/5 along, 3u/5 perpendicular; M1 momentum 4u/5 = v_A + v_B; M1 restitution v_B − v_A = ⅔(4u/5); A1 v_A = 2u/15; A1 v_B = 2u/3; A1 speed of A = √((2u/15)² + (3u/5)²) = √85 u/15.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass 0.4 kg, moving at 3 m s⁻¹, strikes sphere B, of mass 0.6 kg, at rest. A's velocity makes 50° with the line of centres and e = 0.8. Find the speed of B after the collision and the direction in which B moves.
parts.answer: 1.39 m s⁻¹ along the line of centres
parts.working: B1 3cos 50° = 1.93; M1 0.4(1.93) = 0.4v_A + 0.6v_B; M1 v_B − v_A = 0.8(1.93); A1 v_B = 1.39, along the line of centres (B receives an impulse only along that line).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the component of A's velocity perpendicular to the line of centres after the collision, and explain why it is unchanged.
parts.answer: 2.30 m s⁻¹; the spheres are smooth so the impulse acts only along the line of centres
parts.working: B1 3sin 50° value; B1 reason.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Smooth spheres A (mass 3 kg) and B (mass 1 kg) collide when the line of centres is parallel to the unit vector i. Just before impact A has velocity (4i + 3j) m s⁻¹ and B has velocity (−2i + j) m s⁻¹. The coefficient of restitution is 0.5. Find the velocities of A and B just after impact, in vector form.
parts.working: B1 j-components unchanged; M1 3(4) + 1(−2) = 3v_A + v_B; M1 v_B − v_A = 0.5(4 − (−2)); A1 v_A = 1.75; A1 v_B = 4.75.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the impulse on B.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass m, moving with speed u, collides with sphere B, of mass 2m, which is at rest. Before impact A's direction makes an angle of 45° with the line of centres. After the impact A moves perpendicular to the line of centres. Find the coefficient of restitution e.
parts.working: M1 momentum along line mu/√2 = mv_A + 2mv_B; M1 restitution v_B − v_A = e u/√2; M1 v_A = 0 gives v_B = u/(2√2) and v_B = eu/√2; A1 e = ½.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the fraction of the original kinetic energy lost in the collision.
parts.working: M1 KE after = ½m(u/√2)² + ½(2m)(u/(2√2))² = 3mu²/8; M1 loss = ½mu² − 3mu²/8 = mu²/8; A1 fraction ¼.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass 3m, and sphere B, of mass m, are moving towards each other. Immediately before impact, A has speed 4u at 60° to the line of centres and B has speed 2u at 60° to the line of centres, each velocity having a component directed towards the other sphere. The coefficient of restitution is ⅓. Find the components of the velocities of A and B along the line of centres after the impact.
parts.answer: A: u, B: 2u (both in the original direction of A's component)
parts.working: B1 along-line components 2u and −u (taking A→B as positive); M1 3m(2u) + m(−u) = 3mv_A + mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = ⅓(2u + u); A1 v_A = u; A1 v_B = 2u.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of each sphere after the impact and the angle between the direction of motion of B and the line of centres.
parts.working: B1 perpendicular components 2√3u (A) and √3u (B) unchanged; M1 speeds by Pythagoras; A1 √13u and √7u; A1 tan⁻¹(√3/2) = 40.9°.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: On a smooth horizontal floor in a school science lab in Peshawar, sphere A of mass 1 kg moving at 8 m s⁻¹ strikes an identical sphere B at rest. A's velocity makes 30° with the line of centres and e = 0.6. Find the angle through which A's direction of motion is turned by the collision.
parts.working: B1 components 4√3 along, 4 perpendicular; M1 momentum and M1 restitution along line; A1 v_A = 0.2 × 4√3 = 1.39; M1 new angle with line tan⁻¹(4/1.39) = 70.9°; A1 deflection 70.9° − 30° = 40.9°.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two smooth spheres A and B, each of mass m and radius a, lie on a smooth horizontal table. B is at rest. A moves with speed u along a straight line whose perpendicular distance from the centre of B is a. Show that, at impact, A's velocity makes an angle of 30° with the line of centres.
parts.working: M1 distance between centres at impact is 2a; A1 sin α = a/(2a) = ½, α = 30° (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The coefficient of restitution is ½. Find, in terms of u, the speeds of A and B after the impact.
parts.working: M1 momentum along line m(√3u/2) = mv_A + mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = ½(√3u/2); A1 v_A = √3u/8; A1 v_B = 3√3u/8; A1 speed of A √(3/64 + 1/4)u = √19u/8.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the angle between A's direction of motion after the impact and the line of centres.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a snooker club in Lahore, the cue ball (mass 0.17 kg) moving at 2.4 m s⁻¹ strikes a red ball of equal mass at rest. Model the balls as smooth spheres of equal radius. At impact the cue ball's velocity makes 25° with the line of centres, and e = 0.9. Find the speed of the red ball after the impact.
parts.working: B1 2.4cos 25° = 2.18; M1 momentum; M1 restitution; A1 v_B = 0.95 × 2.18 = 2.07.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the impulse between the balls.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the speed of the cue ball after the impact.
parts.working: M1 v_A = 0.05 × 2.18 = 0.109, perpendicular component 2.4sin 25°; A1 1.02.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass 2m, moving with speed u at 30° to the line of centres, strikes sphere B, of mass m, which is at rest. After the impact A moves at 45° to the line of centres. Find the exact value of the coefficient of restitution.
parts.working: B1 components √3u/2 along, u/2 perpendicular; M1 2m(√3u/2) = 2mv_A + mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = e√3u/2; A1 v_A = (2 − e)√3u/6; M1 tan 45° = (u/2)/v_A so v_A = u/2; A1 2 − e = √3, e = 2 − √3.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere B, of mass 4 kg, moving at 3 m s⁻¹, strikes sphere A, of mass 2 kg, which is at rest. B's velocity makes 40° with the line of centres and the coefficient of restitution is 0.25. Find the speed of A after the collision.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of B after the collision and the angle through which its direction of motion is deflected.
parts.working: A1 v_B along = 1.34; M1 speed √(1.34² + 1.93²) = 2.35; M1 angle with line tan⁻¹(1.93/1.34) = 55.2°; A1 deflection 15.2°.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Smooth sphere A, of mass 2 kg, moves with velocity 5i m s⁻¹ and strikes smooth sphere B, of mass 3 kg, at rest. At impact the line of centres is parallel to the vector 3i + 4j. The coefficient of restitution is ½. Find the components of A's velocity along and perpendicular to the line of centres before impact.
parts.answer: Along: 3 m s⁻¹; perpendicular part: (3.2i − 2.4j) m s⁻¹

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the velocities of A and B after the impact, in the form ai + bj.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass 0.5 kg, moving at 6 m s⁻¹ at 40° to the line of centres, collides with sphere B, of mass 1.5 kg, which is moving along the line of centres towards A at 2 m s⁻¹. The coefficient of restitution is 0.4. Find the velocity components of A and B along the line of centres after impact.
parts.answer: A: 2.33 m s⁻¹ reversed (away from B); B: 0.309 m s⁻¹ in A's original direction

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the loss of kinetic energy in the collision.
parts.working: M1 only along-line components change; M1 [½(0.5)(4.60)² + ½(1.5)(2²)] − [½(0.5)(−2.33)² + ½(1.5)(0.309)²]; A1 6.85 J.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass m, moving with speed u, collides with sphere B, of mass km, which is at rest. A's velocity makes an angle α with the line of centres, where sin α = 0.6. The coefficient of restitution is 0.75. After the collision A moves at right angles to its original direction. Show that the component of A's velocity along the line of centres after impact is −0.45u (that is, A's component is reversed).
parts.working: B1 before: (0.8u, 0.6u) along/perpendicular; M1 after: (v, 0.6u), scalar product with original = 0; A1 0.8uv + 0.36u² = 0, v = −0.45u (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of k.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass m, moving with speed u at 60° to the line of centres, strikes sphere B, of mass 3m, which is at rest. The coefficient of restitution is e. Show that A's velocity component along the line of centres is reversed by the collision if and only if e > ⅓.
parts.working: M1 momentum m(u/2) = mv_A + 3mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = eu/2; A1 v_A = (1 − 3e)u/8; A1 v_A < 0 ⇔ e > ⅓ (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that e = ⅔, find the angle between the directions of motion of A before and after the collision.

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass 2m, has velocity of magnitude 5u, with components 3u along the line of centres (towards B) and 4u perpendicular to it. Sphere B, of mass 3m, moves with speed 2u perpendicular to the line of centres. They collide; the coefficient of restitution is ½. Find the speed of B after the collision and the angle its direction makes with the line of centres.
parts.working: M1 2m(3u) = 2mv_A + 3mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = ½(3u); A1 v_A = 0.3u; A1 v_B = 1.8u; M1 combine with 2u perpendicular: √(1.8² + 2²)u = 2.69u; A1 tan⁻¹(2/1.8) = 48.0°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find, in terms of m and u, the loss in kinetic energy.
parts.working: M1 only the along-line components change; M1 ½(2m)(3u)² − [½(2m)(0.3u)² + ½(3m)(1.8u)²]; A1 9 − 0.09 − 4.86 = 4.05, so 4.05mu².

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A moves with speed u at an angle α to the line of centres and strikes an identical sphere B at rest. The coefficient of restitution is e (e < 1). After the impact A moves at an angle β to the line of centres. Show that tan β = 2tan α/(1 − e).
parts.working: M1 momentum u cos α = v_A + v_B; M1 v_B − v_A = eu cos α; A1 v_A = ½(1 − e)u cos α; A1 tan β = u sin α / v_A (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that α = 20° and β = 45°, find e correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why β > α for every value of e with 0 ≤ e < 1.
parts.answer: 2/(1 − e) > 1 so tan β > tan α
parts.working: B1 2/(1 − e) ≥ 2 > 1 and tan is increasing on (0°, 90°).

practice.stem: The spheres are smooth and have equal radii. The line of centres is the line joining their centres at the instant of impact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sphere A, of mass m, moving with speed u at 30° to the line of centres, strikes sphere B, of mass M, which is at rest. The coefficient of restitution is e. After impact, A moves at right angles to its original direction. Show that M/m = 4/(3e − 1).
parts.working: B1 before (√3u/2, u/2); M1 after (v, u/2) with (√3u/2)v + u²/4 = 0, v = −u/(2√3); M1 momentum m(√3u/2) = mv + Mw; M1 w − v = e√3u/2; M1 eliminate w: v = (m − eM)√3u/(2(m + M)); A1 (m − eM)/(m + M) = −⅓ gives 4m = M(3e − 1) (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the least possible value of M/m and state the condition on e for such a deflection to be possible.
parts.answer: Least M/m = 2 (when e = 1); need e > ⅓
parts.working: B1 3e − 1 > 0 so e > ⅓; B1 4/(3e − 1) is least when e = 1, giving 2.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sphere moving on a smooth horizontal floor at 8 m s⁻¹ strikes a vertical wall. Its direction makes 30° with the wall. The coefficient of restitution is 0.5. Find the speed of the sphere after the impact and the angle its new direction makes with the wall.
parts.answer: 7.21 m s⁻¹ at 16.1° to the wall
parts.working: B1 parallel component 8cos 30° = 4√3 unchanged; B1 normal component 8sin 30° = 4; M1 after: 0.5 × 4 = 2; A1 speed √(48 + 4) = √52 = 7.21; A1 tan⁻¹(2/(4√3)) = 16.1°.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sphere of mass 0.2 kg moves on a smooth horizontal surface with velocity (6i − 4j) m s⁻¹ and hits a straight smooth wall which lies along the x-axis. The coefficient of restitution is 0.75. Find the velocity of the sphere after the impact.
parts.working: M1 i-component unchanged, j-component reversed and multiplied by e; A1 6i + 3j.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by the wall and the kinetic energy lost.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sphere approaches a straight vertical cushion with velocity components 3 m s⁻¹ parallel to the cushion and 4 m s⁻¹ perpendicular to it. The coefficient of restitution is 0.25. Find the speed of the sphere after impact and the angle between its path and the cushion.
parts.answer: √10 ≈ 3.16 m s⁻¹ at 18.4° to the cushion
parts.working: B1 perpendicular component 0.25 × 4 = 1; M1 speed √(3² + 1²); A1 √10 = 3.16; A1 tan⁻¹(1/3) = 18.4°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the percentage of kinetic energy lost.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sphere strikes a smooth vertical wall with its path at 45° to the wall and rebounds with its path at 30° to the wall. Find the exact coefficient of restitution.
parts.working: M1 parallel component unchanged: v cos 45°; M1 tan 30° = e v sin 45° / (v cos 45°) = e; A1 e = 1/√3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the fraction of the sphere's kinetic energy lost in the impact.
parts.working: M1 KE ∝ speed²; before v², after v²cos²45°(1 + tan²30°) = v²(½)(4/3) = ⅔v²; A1 loss ⅓v² relative to v², A1 fraction ⅓.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: On a smooth horizontal table, two straight smooth cushions meet at right angles at a corner. A sphere moving at 5 m s⁻¹ strikes one cushion and then the other. The coefficient of restitution for each impact is 0.6. Show that after both impacts the sphere moves parallel to its original path but in the opposite direction.
parts.working: B1 axes along the cushions: velocity (a, b) with a² + b² = 25; M1 first impact (a, −0.6b)… i.e. one component reversed and scaled by 0.6; M1 second impact reverses and scales the other; A1 final velocity (−0.6a, −0.6b) = −0.6 × original (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the final speed and the fraction of the original kinetic energy remaining.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A small smooth sphere falls vertically and hits a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal, with speed 6 m s⁻¹ just before impact. The coefficient of restitution is 0.5. Find the components of the sphere's velocity parallel and perpendicular to the plane immediately after impact.
parts.answer: Parallel: 3 m s⁻¹ down the line of greatest slope; perpendicular: 2.60 m s⁻¹ away from the plane
parts.working: B1 parallel component 6sin 30° = 3 unchanged; B1 normal component 6cos 30° = 3√3; B1 after: 0.5 × 3√3 = 1.5√3 = 2.60.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the sphere immediately after impact and the angle its velocity makes with the plane.
parts.answer: 3.97 m s⁻¹ at 40.9° to the plane

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sphere moving on a smooth horizontal table at 4 m s⁻¹ hits a straight smooth cushion and rebounds with speed 3 m s⁻¹. The coefficient of restitution is 0.5. Find the angle between the sphere's original path and the cushion.
parts.working: B1 components 4cos α and 4sin α; B1 after: 4cos α and 2sin α; M1 16cos²α + 4sin²α = 9; M1 16 − 12sin²α = 9, sin²α = 7/12; A1 α = 49.8°.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sphere hits a smooth wall with its path making an angle α with the wall. The coefficient of restitution is e. Show that the fraction of kinetic energy lost is (1 − e²)sin²α.
parts.working: M1 components v cos α (unchanged) and v sin α → ev sin α; M1 loss ∝ v²sin²α − e²v²sin²α; A1 divide by v² (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that e = 0.6 and that 36% of the kinetic energy is lost, find α.

practice.stem: The sphere is small and smooth, and the barrier (wall, cushion or plane) is smooth and fixed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A ball of mass 0.15 kg, modelled as a small smooth sphere, slides at 10 m s⁻¹ across smooth horizontal ice and strikes a straight vertical barrier, its path making an angle α with the barrier. The coefficient of restitution is 0.64. After the impact the ball moves at right angles to its original path. Show that tan²α = 1/e and find α.
parts.working: B1 before (10cos α, −10sin α); B1 after (10cos α, 10e sin α); M1 scalar product zero: 100cos²α − 100e sin²α = 0; A1 tan²α = 1/e (AG); A1 tan α = 1.25, α = 51.3°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by the barrier on the ball.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two smooth spheres A (mass 3 kg) and B (mass 2 kg), of equal radius, move towards each other along the same straight line with speeds 4 m s⁻¹ and 1 m s⁻¹ respectively, and collide directly. The coefficient of restitution is 0.6. Find the velocities of A and B after the collision.
parts.answer: A: 0.800 m s⁻¹, B: 3.80 m s⁻¹, both in A's original direction

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the kinetic energy lost in the collision.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three smooth spheres A, B and C, of equal radius and masses m, 2m and 4m, lie at rest in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface, in that order. A is projected towards B with speed u. The coefficient of restitution between each pair is e. Find, in terms of e and u, the velocities of A and B after their collision.
parts.working: M1 mu = mv_A + 2mv_B; M1 v_B − v_A = eu; A1 v_A; A1 v_B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B then collides with C. Find the value of e for which B is brought to rest by this collision, and show that A is then also at rest.
parts.working: M1 B–C collision: 2m v_B = 2m w_B + 4m w_C, w_C − w_B = e v_B; M1 w_B = (2 − 4e)v_B/6; A1 w_B = 0 ⇔ e = ½; A1 v_A = (1 − 1)u/3 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: For this value of e, find the total kinetic energy lost in terms of m and u.
parts.working: M1 v_B = u/2, w_C = (1 + e)v_B/3 = u/4; only C moves: ½(4m)(u/4)² = mu²/8; A1 loss ½mu² − mu²/8 = 3mu²/8.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform L-shaped lamina is a sign for a shop in Peshawar. Taking axes along two edges, its vertices are (0, 0), (6, 0), (6, 2), (2, 2), (2, 5) and (0, 5), with units in decimetres. Find the coordinates of the centre of mass of the lamina.
parts.working: M1 split into rectangles: 6 × 2 (area 12, centre (3, 1)) and 2 × 3 (area 6, centre (1, 3.5)); M1 moments: x̄ = (12 × 3 + 6 × 1)/18; A1 x̄ = 7/3; A1 ȳ = (12 × 1 + 6 × 3.5)/18 = 11/6.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform square lamina OABC has side 8 cm. A circular hole of radius 2 cm is cut from it, with its centre at the point 2 cm from both OA and OC. Find the distance of the centre of mass of the remaining lamina from OC, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the distance of the centre of mass from OA, giving a reason.
parts.answer: 4.49 cm, by symmetry about the diagonal OB
parts.working: B1

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A toy is made from a uniform solid cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm joined to a uniform solid hemisphere of radius 3 cm made of the same material, so that the plane face of the hemisphere coincides with one end of the cylinder. Find the distance of the centre of mass of the toy from the free plane end of the cylinder.
parts.working: B1 volumes 90π and 18π; B1 hemisphere centre of mass 3 × 3/8 = 9/8 cm from its plane face, i.e. 10 + 9/8 from the end; M1 (90π × 5 + 18π × 89/8) = 108π x̄; A1 x̄ = 6.02 cm.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rectangular lamina ABCD of mass 2 kg has AB = 0.4 m and BC = 0.3 m. A particle of mass 0.5 kg is attached at C. Find the distances of the centre of mass of the combined body from AB and from AD.
parts.answer: 0.18 m from AB, 0.24 m from AD
parts.working: M1 moments about AD: 2 × 0.2 + 0.5 × 0.4 = 2.5x̄; A1 x̄ = 0.24 m; M1 moments about AB: 2 × 0.15 + 0.5 × 0.3 = 2.5ȳ; A1 ȳ = 0.18 m.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform lamina is formed from a rectangle ABCD, with AB = 12 cm and BC = 4 cm, and a semicircle with diameter DC drawn outside the rectangle. Show that the distance of the centre of mass of the lamina from AB is (40 + 12π)/(8 + 3π) cm.
parts.working: B1 areas 48 and 18π; B1 semicircle centre of mass 4r/(3π) = 8/π from DC; M1 moments about AB: 48 × 2 + 18π(4 + 8/π); M1 divide by 48 + 18π; A1 (240 + 72π)/(48 + 18π) = (40 + 12π)/(8 + 3π).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find this distance correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid cone has base radius 4 cm and height 12 cm. The top part, a cone of height 6 cm with the same vertex, is removed to leave a frustum. Show that the centre of mass of the frustum is 33/14 cm from its larger plane face.
parts.working: B1 volumes in ratio 16 × 12 : 4 × 6 = 192 : 24 (small cone radius 2); B1 centres of mass 3 cm and 6 + 1.5 = 7.5 cm from the base; M1 192 × 3 − 24 × 7.5 = 168x̄; M1 x̄ = 396/168; A1 33/14.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A framework is made from three uniform rods of the same material: AB = 6 m, BC = 8 m and AC = 10 m, forming a right-angled triangle with the right angle at B. Find the distances of the centre of mass of the framework from BC and from AB.
parts.answer: 2 m from BC, 3 m from AB
parts.working: B1 masses proportional to 6, 8, 10 with midpoints (0, 3), (4, 0), (4, 3) taking B as origin, BC along the x-axis; M1 x̄ = (6 × 0 + 8 × 4 + 10 × 4)/24 = 3; M1 ȳ = (6 × 3 + 0 + 10 × 3)/24; A1 2 m from BC and 3 m from AB.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform wire is bent into the shape of a semicircular arc of radius a together with its diameter, forming a closed 'D' shape. Show that the centre of mass is at a distance 2a/(π + 2) from the diameter.
parts.working: B1 arc centre of mass 2a/π from the centre (from a sin α/α with α = π/2); B1 masses ∝ πa and 2a; M1 πa × 2a/π + 2a × 0 = (πa + 2a)ȳ; A1 2a/(π + 2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The shape is freely suspended from one end of the diameter. Find the angle the diameter makes with the vertical.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A lampshade is modelled as a closed hollow cone made from thin uniform sheet metal: a conical curved surface of base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm, together with a circular base of radius 3 cm made from the same sheet. Find the distance of the centre of mass of the lampshade from its base.
parts.working: B1 curved surface area πrl = 15π (slant height 5); B1 its centre of mass is h/3 = 4/3 cm from the base; M1 15π × 4/3 + 9π × 0 = 24π ȳ; A1 5/6 cm.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid hemisphere of radius 2a has a concentric hemisphere of radius a removed, the two plane faces being in the same plane. Show that the centre of mass of the remaining solid is at a distance 45a/56 from the plane face.
parts.working: B1 volumes in ratio 8 : 1; B1 centres of mass 3(2a)/8 = 3a/4 and 3a/8; M1 8 × 3a/4 − 1 × 3a/8 = 7ȳ; M1 6a − 3a/8 = 45a/8; A1 ȳ = 45a/56.

parts.label: b
parts.text: This solid rests in equilibrium with its curved surface on a smooth horizontal plane. Explain why the plane face is horizontal.
parts.answer: The normal reaction passes through the centre O (normal to a sphere), so O and the centre of mass must be in a vertical line; this line is the axis, so the plane face is horizontal
parts.working: B1

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform square lamina OABC has vertices O(0, 0), A(6a, 0), B(6a, 6a) and C(0, 6a). The triangle OPC, where P is the point (ka, 3a) with 0 < k < 6, is removed. Show that the x-coordinate of the centre of mass of the remaining lamina is (108 − k²)a/(36 − 3k).
parts.working: B1 triangle area 3ka² with centroid (ka/3, 3a); M1 36a² × 3a − 3ka² × ka/3 = (36a² − 3ka²)x̄; A1 numerator (108 − k²)a³; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that x̄ = 11a/3, find k.

practice.subtopic: Centre of mass of composite bodies

parts.label: a
parts.text: A child's spinning top is made from a uniform solid cone of height h and base radius r joined at its base to a uniform solid hemisphere of radius r of the same material. Show that the centre of mass of the top is on the axis at a distance (3r² − h²)/(4(h + 2r)) from the common plane face, on the hemisphere side.
parts.working: B1 volumes (1/3)πr²h and (2/3)πr³; B1 centres of mass h/4 (cone side) and 3r/8 (hemisphere side); M1 moments about the plane face with a consistent sign convention; A1 πr²(3r² − h²)/12; A1 divide by πr²(h + 2r)/3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The top is placed with its hemispherical surface on a horizontal table and released from a tilted position. Find the set of values of h, in terms of r, for which it returns to the upright position.
parts.working: M1 needs the centre of mass inside the hemisphere (below the centre of the hemisphere's plane face), i.e. 3r² − h² > 0; A1 h < √3 r.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rectangular lamina ABCD has AB = 8 cm, BC = 4 cm and mass 3 kg. A particle of mass 1 kg is fixed at C. Find the distances of the centre of mass of the combined body from AD and from AB.
parts.answer: 5 cm from AD, 2.5 cm from AB

parts.label: b
parts.text: The body is freely suspended from A. Find the angle that AB makes with the vertical.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid hemisphere is freely suspended from a point A on the rim of its plane face. Find the angle between the plane face and the vertical.
parts.working: B1 centre of mass 3r/8 from O along the axis; M1 tan θ = (3r/8)/r; A1 20.6°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid cylinder of diameter 8 cm and height 20 cm stands on a rough plane. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. The angle of inclination of the plane is slowly increased. Show that the cylinder slides before it topples, and state the angle at which it starts to slide.
parts.working: M1 sliding when tan α = μ = 0.3, α = 16.7°; M1 toppling when the centre of mass is vertically above the lowest edge: tan α = 4/10; A1 α = 21.8°; A1 16.7° < 21.8°, so it slides first, at 16.7°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm stands on a plane inclined at α to the horizontal. The plane is rough enough to prevent sliding. Find the greatest value of α for which the cylinder does not topple.
parts.working: M1 centre of mass 5 cm above the base on the axis; M1 tan α = 3/5; A1 31.0°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A second cylinder of the same height is made from the same material and stands on the same plane at α = 40°. Find the least radius it must have so that it does not topple.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid frustum has a larger base of radius 4 cm and its centre of mass is 33/14 cm from that base. It stands on its larger base on a rough plane inclined at α to the horizontal. Assuming it does not slide, find the greatest value of α for which it does not topple.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The coefficient of friction between the frustum and the plane is 0.8. The angle α is gradually increased from zero. Determine whether the frustum slides or topples first.
parts.working: M1 sliding when tan α = 0.8, α = 38.7°; A1 38.7° < 59.5°, slides first.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid cone of base radius 4 cm and height 12 cm is freely suspended from a point on the rim of its base. Find the angle between the axis of the cone and the vertical.
parts.working: B1 centre of mass 3 cm from the base on the axis; M1 tan θ = 4/3; A1 53.1°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Instead the cone is placed with its base on a rough plane inclined at β, and it is on the point of toppling. Find β.
parts.working: M1 tan β = 4/3 (same geometry: centre of mass vertically above the lowest point of the rim); A1 53.1°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform square lamina ABCD of side 2a has mass M. A particle of mass m is attached at B. The lamina is freely suspended from A and hangs in equilibrium with AB making an angle tan⁻¹(1/2) with the vertical. Find m in terms of M.
parts.working: M1 take A as origin, AB along x-axis: x̄ = (Ma + 2am)/(M + m); A1 ȳ = Ma/(M + m); M1 tan θ = ȳ/x̄ = M/(M + 2m); M1 M/(M + 2m) = 1/2; A1 m = M/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform cuboid packing crate stands on rough horizontal ground. Its weight is 200 N, its height is 1.2 m and its square base has side 0.6 m. A horizontal force of magnitude P N is applied at the midpoint of a top edge, perpendicular to that edge. Find the value of P at which the crate would be on the point of tipping, assuming it does not slide.
parts.working: M1 moments about the lower edge on the far side: P × 1.2 = 200 × 0.3; A1 equation; A1 P = 50.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The coefficient of friction between the crate and the ground is μ. Find the set of values of μ for which the crate tips over before it slides, as P is gradually increased.
parts.working: M1 sliding needs P > 200μ; M1 tipping first requires 50 < 200μ; A1 μ > 0.25.

parts.label: c
parts.text: If instead the force is applied at height h m above the ground (0 < h ≤ 1.2), find the set of values of h for which the crate tips before it slides when μ = 0.4.
parts.working: M1 tipping when P × h = 200 × 0.3, so P = 60/h; sliding when P = 0.4 × 200 = 80; M1 tips first if 60/h < 80; A1 h > 0.75 m (up to the top of the crate, 1.2 m).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid hemisphere of radius r rests in equilibrium with its curved surface in contact with a rough plane inclined at α to the horizontal. Show that the plane face of the hemisphere makes an angle θ with the horizontal, where sin θ = (8/3) sin α.
parts.working: M1 the reaction (normal and friction) acts at the contact point; for equilibrium the centre of mass G is vertically above the contact point; M1 the normal at the contact point passes through the centre O, so the horizontal distance from O to G equals r sin α; A1 OG sin θ = r sin α with OG = 3r/8; A1 sin θ = (8/3) sin α.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find θ when α = 15°, and find the greatest value of α for which such an equilibrium is possible (assuming friction is sufficient).

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the least possible coefficient of friction when α = 15°.
parts.working: B1 friction resolves along the plane: F = W sin α, R = W cos α, μ ≥ tan α.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rectangular lamina OABC has vertices O(0, 0), A(8a, 0), B(8a, 4a) and C(0, 4a). The triangle with vertices A, B and P(6a, 2a) is removed. Find the coordinates of the centre of mass of the remaining lamina.
parts.working: B1 triangle area 4a², centroid (22a/3, 2a); M1 x̄ = (32a² × 4a − 4a² × 22a/3)/28a²; A1 x̄ = 74a/21, ȳ = 2a by symmetry about y = 2a.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The remaining lamina is freely suspended from O. Find the angle between OA and the vertical.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The lamina is instead held in a vertical plane with the edge OA in contact with a rough horizontal surface, and is slowly tilted in its own plane about A. Find the angle through which it can be turned before it topples.
parts.working: M1 horizontal distance of G from A is 8a − 74a/21 = 94a/21, height 2a; A1 tan φ = 2/(94/21) = 21/47, φ = 24.1°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform ladder of length 5 m and mass 20 kg rests with its foot on rough horizontal ground and its top against a smooth vertical wall. The ladder makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Take g = 10 m s⁻². Find the magnitude of the reaction at the wall.
parts.working: M1 moments about the foot: S × 5 sin 60° = 200 × 2.5 cos 60°; A1 equation; A1 S = 57.7 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least possible value of the coefficient of friction between the ladder and the ground.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform plank AB of length 4 m and weight 300 N rests with end A on rough horizontal ground and is supported by a smooth peg at C, where AC = 3 m. The plank is inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Find the magnitude of the force exerted by the peg on the plank.
parts.working: B1 the peg force is perpendicular to the plank; M1 moments about A: R × 3 = 300 × 2 cos 30°; A1 R = 173 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the normal reaction and the friction force at A, and hence find the least possible coefficient of friction.
parts.answer: Normal reaction 150 N, friction 86.6 N, μ ≥ 1/√3 ≈ 0.577
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: N + R cos 30° = 300, N = 150; M1 resolve horizontally: F = R sin 30° = 86.6; M1 μ ≥ F/N; A1 0.577.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform ladder of length 6 m and weight 150 N rests on rough horizontal ground, coefficient of friction 0.4, against a smooth vertical wall. The ladder makes an angle of 65° with the ground. A painter of weight 700 N climbs the ladder. Find how far up the ladder he can climb before the ladder slips, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 R = 850 N; B1 F_max = 0.4 × 850 = 340 N, so wall reaction S = 340 N at limiting equilibrium; M1 moments about the foot: S × 6 sin 65° = 150 × 3 cos 65° + 700d cos 65°; M1 rearrange for d; A1 d = (2040 tan 65° − 450)/700; A1 5.61 m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rod AB of length 1.2 m and mass 3 kg has end A in contact with a rough vertical wall. The rod is held horizontal, perpendicular to the wall, by a light string attached to B and to a point C on the wall 0.9 m vertically above A. Take g = 10 m s⁻². Find the tension in the string.
parts.working: B1 string length 1.5 m, sin(angle ABC) = 0.6; M1 moments about A: T × 0.6 × 1.2 = 30 × 0.6; A1 T = 25 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least possible coefficient of friction between the rod and the wall.
parts.working: M1 horizontal: normal reaction = T cos = 25 × 0.8 = 20 N; M1 vertical: F = 30 − 25 × 0.6 = 15 N; A1 μ ≥ 15/20 = 0.75.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform ladder rests in limiting equilibrium with its foot on rough horizontal ground (coefficient of friction μ₁) and its top against a rough vertical wall (coefficient of friction μ₂). The ladder makes an angle θ with the ground. Show that tan θ = (1 − μ₁μ₂)/(2μ₁).
parts.working: M1 at both contacts friction is limiting: F₁ = μ₁R, F₂ = μ₂S; M1 horizontally S = μ₁R, vertically R + μ₂S = W, giving R = W/(1 + μ₁μ₂); M1 moments about the foot: S × 2a sin θ + μ₂S × 2a cos θ = W a cos θ; A1 substitute S; A1 tan θ = (1 − μ₁μ₂)/(2μ₁).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find θ when μ₁ = 0.5 and μ₂ = 0.25.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rod AB of weight W has end A on rough horizontal ground. The rod is held at 40° to the horizontal by a light string attached at B, the string being perpendicular to the rod and in the same vertical plane. Find the tension in the string in terms of W.
parts.working: M1 moments about A, rod length 2a: T × 2a = W a cos 40°; A1 equation; A1 T = 0.383W.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least possible coefficient of friction at A, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 the string pulls at 40° to the vertical, towards A's side horizontally: horizontal component T sin 40°, vertical T cos 40°; M1 N = W − T cos 40° = W(1 − cos²40°/2); M1 F = T sin 40°; A1 μ ≥ sin 40° cos 40°/(2 − cos²40°) = 0.348.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rod AB of length 2a and weight W hangs below a fixed rough horizontal wire. End A is attached to a small light ring threaded on the wire, and a horizontal force P, in the vertical plane containing the wire, is applied at B. The rod rests in equilibrium at an angle θ to the vertical. Show that P = (W/2) tan θ.
parts.working: M1 moments about A; A1 P × 2a cos θ = W × a sin θ; A1 P = (W/2) tan θ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The coefficient of friction between the ring and the wire is 0.35. Find the greatest value of θ for which equilibrium is possible.
parts.working: M1 resolving vertically for the whole system: normal reaction at the ring = W; M1 horizontally: friction = P; M1 limiting: (W/2) tan θ = 0.35W, tan θ = 0.7; A1 θ = 35.0°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform ladder rests with its foot on rough horizontal ground and its top against a rough vertical wall. The coefficient of friction is μ at both contacts. The ladder is on the point of slipping when it makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Find the exact value of μ.
parts.working: M1 resolve: S = μR and R + μS = W; M1 moments about the foot: S × 2a sin 60° + μS × 2a cos 60° = Wa cos 60°; M1 obtain tan 60° = (1 − μ²)/(2μ); A1 μ² + 2√3μ − 1 = 0; M1 quadratic formula; A1 μ = 2 − √3 (positive root).
